limitations: Selectors are not all independently observed: provenance distinguishes literal, template expansion and authored adaptation.
Source SDK and GOL versions vary; all proposed cases need validation against our pinned GOL 2.0 data and reference.
Bounding-box kernels do not reproduce radius, polygon, network or export workflows.
No proposed cases have been executed; cardinalities, result equivalence and timing remain unknown.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Zoom/pan map-layer workload
steps: At fixed z6 and z7 tiles execute the source layer selector sets; at z12 use broad bbox selection and client layer dispatch.
Decode tags and geometry together, checksum layer membership and geometry; pan over 16 adjacent tiles and return to the first tile.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Combined-consumer/session harness; coordinate clipping and vector-tile encoding are separate optional end-to-end costs.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Do not extrapolate the low-zoom selector list to all zoom levels. Include London, Highlands and Cornwall sessions.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Road graph extraction
steps: Select w[highway] and n[highway] in Birmingham and Lake District windows.
Consume way tags, ordered node IDs, coordinates and tagged-node controls; deduplicate shared node IDs.
Trim contiguous in-bounds node runs, classify ways, and checksum graph nodes/edges.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Combined-consumer harness using existing way-node identity and tag APIs; verify input was built with retained node IDs.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Separate source-like materialization from streaming Rust implementation; verify identical graph output. Do not replace shared IDs with coordinate equality.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Neighbourhood street gazetteer
steps: Use the notebook Campsbourne bbox and w[highway][name].
Consume names and geometry together; checksum name groups.
Optionally benchmark GeoJSON serialization and dissolve by name separately.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Combined tags/geometry consumer; dissolve/serialization adapters only for full pipeline.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Repeat in equivalent small neighbourhood windows in Cardiff and Edinburgh; these additional windows are authored adaptations.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Repeated peak scans for multiple start towns
steps: Select start settlements, then n[natural=peak,volcano,hill][ele].
Consume elevation, coordinates, name:cs/name:en/name fallback; retain the source ele<9000 consumer predicate.
Repeat peak enumeration for a fixed recorded set of start towns; optionally compute distance ordering and rising elevation sequence.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Repeated enumeration and projected-field consumer harness; geodesic/distance ranking is additional application work.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Source scans peaks repeatedly; UK population/height variants are explicitly authored. Pin settlement IDs after discovery rather than silently picking first traversal results.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Platforms without nearby platform ways
steps: Select n[public_transport=platform].
For each node seek platform-way candidates within 15 m; stop at first exact match.
Return candidate IDs with no matching nearby way.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Exact distance predicate and dependent-query harness required for end-to-end equivalence.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: A bbox is a broad phase only. Preserve the source w selector; report a separate wa variant if testing platform areas.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Sidewalk consistency
steps: Select w[highway][sidewalk=both,left,right,yes].
For each road seek w[footway=sidewalk] within 10 m.
Read geometry to determine side and parallelism.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Do not claim that bounding-box intersection reproduces this quality rule.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Repeated radius/existence queries
steps: Use a fixed 64 by 64 point grid over a city and a rural window; apply the XML layers in source order.
Use exact radius filtering, short-circuit on a hit, and inspect lanes/cables where the layer requires it.
Freeze or omit probabilistic rendering with an explicitly documented deterministic checksum.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Exact radius filtering and existence/session harness required.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: The 4096 grid points form one correlated application session, not 4096 independent benchmark families. Chain the positive and negative highway predicates.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Area index and interactive name search
steps: Read named administrative boundaries and named place nodes once, including admin_level and bounds.
Build the source-like normalized name index; separately time repeated searches with limit 10.
Run bbox *[name] searches with application Unicode normalization and first-10 output.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Index-building and application-normalization consumer harness; reader supplies fields/bounds.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Do not benchmark a prebuilt application index as GOL scan performance or substitute case-sensitive GOQL substring matching for normalized search.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Building entrances and bus-route parents
steps: Seed buildings/residential streets using pinned IDs discovered outside timed runs.
Traverse building nodes and filter entrance tags; traverse street parent relations and filter route=bus.
Consume IDs, tags and member roles where applicable.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Dependent traversal/filter consumer harness using supported relationship primitives.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Current independent members/parents kernels cover primitives but not the full dependent traversal. Existence and all-results variants should be reported separately.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Projection, relation expansion and top-N
steps: Compare IDs-only, selected tags, all tags, geometry, relation members/roles and parents in identical windows.
Add park-area top-10 ordering and relation-member expansion variants.
Separate result scanning from JSONB/SQL/geometry conversion.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Projection consumer harness; planar/geodesic area definition and SQL adapters required for full top-N comparison.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: SQL tag-key existence is not automatically identical to GOQL truthy [key]; area ways/relations also differ from r-only scans.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Polygon extraction and export
steps: Use a pinned London polygon plus authored coastal and rural polygons.
Select polygon candidates, consume tags/geometry/relation dependencies.
Optionally serialize XML and run equivalent clipping/PBF conversion in an end-to-end lane.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Exact polygon semantics, export dependency closure and serialization adapters required.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: The current * bbox cases measure the candidate stage only; preserve boundary-crossing ways/relations and explicit clipping contract.

proposed_application_workflows.title: Radius-based light positions
steps: Use authored n[highway=street_lamp] filters at pinned UK centres and 100/500/2000 m radii.
Read point positions, compare first-hit and full enumeration.
Include a count-then-enumerate variant to expose the source two-pass pattern.
proposed_application_workflows.requirements: Exact distance filter and session harness required; bbox kernel is available.
proposed_application_workflows.notes: Prototype source appears to replace its tag-filtered features with world.maxMetersFromLonLat. Intended filtered-light variant is an adaptation, not a literal behavioural reproduction.
